raw_response:
I'll think this through like I do every spring, sitting with my wife figuring out what we'll spend.

My land is 6.5 mu total. Like most years, I keep 1 mu near the house for chili — that land is close to the well so I can water it often, and chili brings more money per mu than grain. The other 5.5 mu I use for the wheat-maize rotation, same as everyone here in Quzhou.

**Wheat (5.5 mu, winter):**
I already planted last October, standard here. I used the Jimai improved variety, same as my neighbor Old Wang — he got 480 kg/mu last year. For base fertilizer I put down about 40 kg of diammonium phosphate per mu and 15 kg of urea before sowing. That gives me roughly 13 kg N and 8 kg P per mu. Then at greening in March I topdress 15 kg urea per mu (about 7 kg more N). Potash I add 5 kg/mu — the input dealer told me wheat needs some K but I don't spend much on it.

Irrigation: winter water in December, then greening water, jointing water, and grain-filling water — 4 times. If spring rain is good I might skip one, but usually not. Pesticide: once for aphids and powdery mildew around April, once for wheat midge. 2 sprays is enough if I catch it early.

**Maize (5.5 mu, summer):**
After wheat harvest in June I plant Zhengdan 958 or similar hybrid directly into the stubble — no-tillage, everybody does it now to save time and get the maize in before the rains. I apply 30 kg compound fertilizer (15-15-15) per mu at sowing, then topdress 20 kg urea per mu at big trumpet stage. That's about 14 kg N, 5 kg P, 5 kg K per mu total. Maize gets rain in July-August so I only irrigate 1-2 times, usually once after sowing if dry. Spray once for corn borer. Expect 550 kg/mu.

**Chili (1 mu, spring-summer):**
This is where I spend most of my money because it pays back. I buy hybrid seedlings from the market — about 300 yuan worth. I plough this mu properly, not rotary, and put down 2 bags of compound fertilizer (about 100 kg) plus some chicken manure I get cheap. During growth I topdress urea 3 times. Total roughly 25 kg N, 12 kg P, 18 kg K per mu. Chili needs water every week or so in summer — I irrigate 7 times. Pests are the problem — aphids, thrips, anthracnose — I spray 5 times at least. Last year I got around 1800 kg/mu of fresh chili.

I don't change much from last year because last year's harvest was fine. Fertilizer prices are still high so I stay with what I know works.
